caption:
Jensen Huang quit as Nvidia CEO on November 12, and some of his own employees want him back.
An internal post asking the board to reconsider drew more than 1,600 comments, according to WIRED.
Flowers and candles also appeared outside Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara.

Should a CEO get a second chance after a scandal like this?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Standard, citing WIRED · Photo: AFP

paragraphs.text: Some Nvidia employees are urging the company's board to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned as president, chief executive and board member on November 12, 2026. WIRED reported, based on internal correspondence it reviewed, that a staff post asking directors to reconsider drew more than 1,600 comments, most of them supportive of Huang, according to summaries of that report by AI Weekly and The Standard.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it for 33 years. His departure followed reports of extramarital affairs, which he acknowledged in a message to employees days earlier, according to Oneindia. The board named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO, and former Synopsys chief Harvey Jones became chair.
A suggestion box thread with 1,600 replies

The push began before the resignation. A longtime Nvidia engineer used the company's internal suggestion box to ask the board to weigh employee sentiment before deciding Huang's future, SBS News reported, citing WIRED. The engineer asked directors to share the findings of their inquiry with staff and to formally collect feedback on whether Huang should stay.

Several replies asked the board to find a way to bring Huang back. One anonymous comment read, "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss." Another said, "We are all humans and can make mistakes," and argued that Huang deserved a second chance, according to The Standard and Oneindia.

Support also spilled outside the company's internal tools. About two dozen employees posted messages backing Huang on LinkedIn in the hours after he stepped down, and one employee sent a companywide email calling for transparency about the circumstances of his exit, Oneindia and AI Weekly reported.
Flowers at headquarters and an all hands meeting

Bouquets of flowers and candles appeared outside Nvidia's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, with no messages attached, SBS News reported, citing CNBC. Some employees cried when the resignation was announced, according to the same report. The Standard published AFP photos of the scene dated November 12.

Kress told employees on November 12 that "You are our greatest strength" and announced an all hands meeting for November 18 to discuss the company's plans, according to SBS News. None of the reports reviewed included a statement from the board on the employee requests.

Employees also want directors to explain why Huang left before the board's investigation was complete, AI Weekly reported. Huang ran the company with a very flat structure, with about 60 senior executives reporting directly to him, and never named a successor, SBS News noted.

The reaction shows how closely Nvidia's identity is tied to its founder. A flat structure with dozens of direct reports and no named successor leaves an interim leader with little room for error, and a vocal group of staff questioning the process adds pressure on a board that already faces investors, lawmakers and investigators. Employee petitions rarely reverse a board decision on their own, but they can shape how directors explain that decision and who they pick next.
The November 18 all hands meeting is the next point to watch: whether Kress and the board address the reinstatement requests or the status of the investigation directly.
